$comment: Typeface pairings shared by every approach. All are free Google Fonts (SIL Open Font License, except a few Apache-2.0 accent fonts noted per family), so they work on the web, in print and in Figma/Adobe after installing. A product picks one in products/<product>/brand.json -> typography.pairing. How well each suits a style is rated in approaches/<id>/typography.json (fit), not here. Designer credits come from Google Fonts listings and the designers' repositories.

pairings.name: Warm Modern
pairings.mood: Friendly and current. The headline face has slightly irregular, ink-trap details that echo hand-drawn line; the body face is open and calm.
pairings.bestFor: Most brands. Posters, social, websites.

display.notes: Started as a fork of Mayenne Sans (Jérémy Landes); influenced by Antique Olive and Grotesque Nº9.

pairings.name: Modern Editorial
pairings.mood: Quiet and elegant. A condensed, high-contrast serif for big headlines over a crisp, neutral sans.
pairings.bestFor: Culture, design, publishing, premium services. Big poster headlines.

display.case: Sentence case; italic for one emphasised word
display.notes: Regular and italic only.

pairings.name: Humanist Classic
pairings.mood: Calm, trustworthy, extremely readable. A true humanist superfamily: serif, sans and mono designed together.
pairings.bestFor: Education, health, non-profits, long reading, anything with lots of text.

pairings.name: Friendly
pairings.mood: Soft and approachable without being childish. A warm, chunky serif headline with a round, modern sans.
pairings.bestFor: Food, hospitality, family, local businesses.

display.notes: Single weight; inspired by Plantin Infant and ITC Italian Old Style.

body.notes: Made for Moldova; on Google Fonts since 2023.

pairings.name: Soft Rounded
pairings.mood: Rounded terminals that echo rounded corners and organic shapes. Friendly and very clear; keep it to bold headlines and a plainer body so it never turns childish.
pairings.bestFor: Health, wellbeing, apps, community services.

display.notes: Rounded terminals.

body.designer: Jacques Le Bailly (from Vernon Adams's Nunito)

pairings.name: Calligraphic Humanist
pairings.mood: The most 'hand-made' of the set: letterforms built from a broad-nib pen. Literary and warm.
pairings.bestFor: Books, crafts, wellbeing, storytelling brands.

body.style: Humanist sans from the same family

pairings.name: Single-Family Minimal
pairings.mood: One family, strict and modern; hierarchy comes from size and weight only. The most minimal option.
pairings.bestFor: Tech, products, studios that want maximum restraint.

pairings.name: Soft Serif
pairings.mood: Bouncy, soft-cornered serif with a gentle humanist sans. Charming; use with restraint (one weight, no 'wonky' extras).
pairings.bestFor: Lifestyle, kids' education, independent shops.

pairings.name: Technical Humanist
pairings.mood: Engineered but warm: a grotesque with humanist touches, with matching serif and mono. Precise without feeling cold.
pairings.bestFor: Science, data, B2B, reports.

pairings.name: Geometric (Jost)
pairings.mood: Clean, constructed and calm. One geometric family inspired by 1920s German sans-serifs, used bold for headlines and regular for text: hierarchy from size and weight alone.
pairings.bestFor: Bauhaus-style posters, architecture, furniture, design studios, culture, education.

display.case: Sentence case, or all lowercase for headlines
display.notes: Described by its designer as inspired by the 1920s German sans-serifs; an original interpretation in the Futura tradition, not a copy. Variable since version 3.0.

body.notes: Small x-height for a text face: set body one step larger than with a grotesque (17-18 px on screen).

pairings.name: Heavy Geometric
pairings.mood: Loud and direct. A heavy early-20th-century geometric sans for headlines over Jost for text. For posters that need to be read from across a room.
pairings.bestFor: Events, posters, signage, campaigns with one big message.

display.case: Sentence case, or all lowercase for headlines
display.designer: Matt Bailey and Tyler Finck (The League of Moveable Type)
display.notes: Based on Matt Bailey's Spartan, itself based on early 20th-century American geometric sans-serifs (ATF Spartan). Variable since 2020.

pairings.name: Deco Marquee
pairings.mood: A high-contrast Art Deco display face for the brand word, with a geometric sans for everything else. Glamour kept to one word.
pairings.bestFor: Travel, hotels, theatre and cinema, drinks, events.

display.case: Capitals or title for the brand word only (1-3 words); never for sentences
display.notes: Single weight (400). Extreme contrast: use at 24 px / 18 pt and above.

body.notes: Jost 700 sets the slogan; Limelight sets only the brand word.

pairings.name: Bazaar Editorial
pairings.mood: Didone display over geometric sans: the 1930s fashion-magazine pairing. Elegant, high contrast, lots of white space.
pairings.bestFor: Fashion, beauty, editorial, galleries, premium goods.

display.case: Sentence case; italic for one emphasised word
display.notes: Use the large optical size for headlines; hairlines break up below about 18 px at small opsz settings.

pairings.name: Mid-century Advertising
pairings.mood: Confident and warm. A heavy geometric sans in the American Spartan and Futura tradition over a Caslon drawn from 1950s advertising lettering, with a lively italic for subheads.
pairings.bestFor: Most mid-century work: posters, book and packaging design, websites, editorial.

display.case: Sentence case; letter-spaced capitals for labels
display.designer: Matt Bailey, Tyler Finck (The League of Moveable Type)
display.notes: The League of Moveable Type's interpretation of Matt Bailey's Spartan, based on early 20th-century American geometric sans serifs (ATF and Linotype Spartan were Futura competitors).

body.notes: Based on hand-lettering artists' interpretations of Caslon typical of 1950s advertising, not on 18th-century specimens. Companion display family: Libre Caslon Display (Impallari Type).

pairings.name: Album Cover
pairings.mood: Playful and loud for a few words, calm for the rest. Boogaloo's drawn letters follow 1960s LP-cover lettering; Jost is a clean Futura-style sans for everything else.
pairings.bestFor: Music, food, events, children's products, packaging; short headlines only.

display.case: Sentence case; headlines of six words or fewer
display.notes: Structure of classic American lettering found on 1960s LP covers of Latin music. Single weight; never for body or more than one line of six words.

body.notes: Inspired by 1920s German sans serifs (the Futura tradition); variable since 2020 with Mirko Velimirovic.

pairings.name: Cut and Paste
pairings.mood: Newspaper headline cut into strips, with typewritten labels. Bold, plain and documentary; the default for this approach.
pairings.bestFor: Scrapbook posters, social collage, zines, events, local businesses.

display.style: Grotesque with a width axis, from extra condensed to expanded
display.notes: Use widths 75-100 for headline strips; heavy weights survive rotation and overlap.

pairings.name: Zine
pairings.mood: A tall, condensed poster headline in sentence case, a friendly grotesque for text, and a worn typewriter for labels. Loud but legible.
pairings.bestFor: Music, events, campaigns, youth brands, flyers.

display.notes: Single weight; very tall x-height. Keep headlines to 2-3 strips. The mono, Special Elite (Astigmatic), is a worn typewriter face under the Apache License 2.0 rather than OFL (still free for commercial use); labels and stamps only, never body text.

body.style: Grotesque, slightly wide, optimised for screen at text sizes

pairings.name: Clippings
pairings.mood: A heavy, high-contrast serif like a magazine headline, with a clean sans and a quiet mono. For softer, journal-like collage.
pairings.bestFor: Lifestyle, food, travel, gifts, journaling products.

display.case: Sentence case; italic for one emphasised word
display.notes: Use at 28 px / 20 pt and above, on clean paper strips; hairlines are thin.

pairings.name: Bazaar Signboard
pairings.mood: Bold, high-contrast display letters like a hand-painted cinema hoarding or shop sign, with a calm humanist body. Latin and Devanagari designed to sit together.
pairings.bestFor: Posters, packaging, food, fashion and cultural events in this style; bilingual Latin and Hindi or Marathi headlines.

display.designer: Indian Type Foundry (Devanagari: Tim Donaldson and Jyotish Sonowal; Latin: Shiva Nallaperumal)
display.notes: Single weight that is already heavy. Latin recalls 19th-century poster lettering. Very tall x-height; use at large sizes on screen. On Google Fonts since 2014.

body.designer: Ek Type (Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap)
body.notes: Seven static weights (200-800). Sister families: Mukta Vaani (Gujarati), Mukta Mahee (Gurmukhi), Mukta Malar (Tamil).

pairings.name: Painted Railway Sign
pairings.mood: Brush-cut display letters from Mumbai's hand-painted railway signs over a rounded, friendly body. Warm, local, a little playful.
pairings.bestFor: Street food, cafés, community events, kids and family brands, social posts.

display.notes: Inspired by hand-painted Mumbai railway signs; the Latin borrows the Devanagari brush angle. Single weight. On Google Fonts since 2016.

body.notes: Variable weight. Sister families cover nine Indic scripts plus Arabic (Baloo Bhai 2, Baloo Paaji 2, Baloo Thambi 2, etc.).

pairings.name: Matchbox Geometric
pairings.mood: Heavy geometric letters like a modern matchbox or sticker label, with a humanist body for reading.
pairings.bestFor: Apps, launches, fashion and music in a pop-maximal register; labels and stickers.

display.designer: Indian Type Foundry (Latin: Jonny Pinhorn; Devanagari: Ninad Kale)
display.notes: Nine static weights with italics. One of the first Devanagari typefaces with a full range of weights. On Google Fonts since 2015.

body.designer: Ek Type (Girish Dalvi and Yashodeep Gholap)

pairings.name: Surf Shop
pairings.mood: Fat, brush-born display letters like a hand-painted board-shop sign, over a rounded, friendly sans. The default for this approach.
pairings.bestFor: Posters, merch, social, packaging for playful consumer brands.

display.style: Heavy rounded display inspired by broad-brush lettering
display.case: Sentence case; capitals for 1-3 word stickers
display.notes: One weight only. On Google Fonts since 2012.

body.designer: Hubert and Fischer (with Meir Sadan, Cyreal, Daniel Grumer, Omaima Dajani)

pairings.name: Sticker Script
pairings.mood: A bold, curvy, italic display with bounce, for slapped-on stickers and logotypes; the most 'rad' option. Use for headlines of five words or fewer.
pairings.bestFor: Logotypes, stickers, short headlines, event posters.

display.notes: Latin and Gujarati; drawn from hand-painted Gujarati street lettering. One weight. On Google Fonts since 2016. Respect its origin: do not use the Gujarati glyphs as decoration.

body.designer: Hubert and Fischer (with Meir Sadan, Cyreal, Daniel Grumer, Omaima Dajani)

pairings.name: Board Shorts
pairings.mood: A sturdy, slightly condensed humanist display that fits long headlines on a tilt, with a soft, clear body. The calmest option for text-heavier work.
pairings.bestFor: Web pages, banners, longer headlines, menus and price lists.

display.notes: One weight. On Google Fonts since 2012.

body.designer: Vernon Adams, Jacques Le Bailly, Manvel Shmavonyan, Alexei Vanyashin

pairings.name: Protest Poster
pairings.mood: Loud, urgent and plain. A tall, condensed advertising gothic for big headlines over a sturdy grotesque with width and weight axes.
pairings.bestFor: Posters, gig and event posters, social posts, campaigns that need to shout clearly.

display.case: Sentence case; capitals only for labels of one to three words
display.notes: A reworking of a traditional advertising sans serif, reshaped for screens. One weight only: hierarchy comes from size. The related family Antonio, built from Anton, adds weights.

body.style: Grotesque with width and weight axes
body.designer: Héctor Gatti and the Omnibus-Type team
body.notes: Omnibus-Type is a collective foundry in Buenos Aires. Archivo Narrow and Archivo Black are sister families; the condensed widths (wdth 62-75) can also set subheads.

pairings.name: Civic Gothic
pairings.mood: Public and confident. A condensed American gothic built for a city's signs and posters, over a slightly rounded grotesque drawn from California road signs.
pairings.bestFor: Civic, transport, sport and community campaigns; events; outdoor and wayfinding-like pieces.

display.case: Sentence case; capitals only for labels
display.notes: Made for the City of Chicago's design system; its tall forms draw on Chicago's railway, political and dance history. Sister families Big Shoulders Stencil and Inline exist; Google Fonts also serves a combined 'Big Shoulders' family.

body.style: Low-contrast grotesque with slightly rounded forms
body.notes: Static family in three widths (Barlow, Semi Condensed, Condensed), 9 weights each; based on California's plates, highway signs, buses and trains.

pairings.name: Marker Talk
pairings.mood: A marker hand that is designed to be read: monoline, unjoined, with Bounce and Informality axes that make repeated letters vary. Figtree keeps body text calm.
pairings.bestFor: Doodles headlines, labels and annotations; social posts, posters, playful landing pages.

display.style: Marker-style handwriting sans with bounce and informality axes
display.designer: Shantell Martin, Arrow Type (Stephen Nixon), Anya Danilova
display.notes: A marker-style font based on the artwork, handwriting and creative philosophy of artist Shantell Martin, built for typographic play and animation (Arrow Type README). Use BNCE 30-60 and INFM 50-100 for headlines (needs the rlig feature on for randomisation); INFM 0 for labels at small sizes. On Google Fonts since 2023.

pairings.name: Notebook Hand
pairings.mood: A quick, teenage-notebook marker hand over a warm humanist sans from the same designer, so the two share proportions.
pairings.bestFor: Sketchnote pages, menus, education, friendly local brands.

display.notes: Single weight; described by its designer as an interpretation of a teenager's handwriting. On Google Fonts since 2011. Headlines and labels only.

scale.$comment: Type sizes are steps of a ratio from the base size. Names match roles used by the templates.

rules: Two families at most (display + body), plus a mono for small data such as dates, prices and codes.
Sentence case everywhere. All capitals only for short labels of one to three words, with letter-spacing.
Three sizes per piece is usually enough: headline, body, small.
Big headlines get tight leading (about 1.0) and slightly negative tracking; body text gets 1.5 leading and lines of 45-75 characters.
Left-align text. Centre only one or two short lines on a centred poster.
No handwriting or marker fonts: the human hand lives in the illustration, not the type.
Match headline weight to the illustration: the stems of headline letters should be about as thick as the ink line.
